title: Eastern Contra Temple
summary: An outward-facing shrine offered a setting for petitioning royal and divine images.
orientation: East of the Akhmenu, facing outward to the east.

claims.text: An outward-facing shrine offered a setting for petitioning royal and divine images.
The shrine’s public-facing role complicates any blanket claim that ordinary worshippers had no contact with temple divinities. It does not imply unrestricted inner-sanctuary access.
The calcite naos held a broken royal/divine dyad; the original royal identity has been debated.

caveats: Field access and demonstration viewpoints are unverified; this is an editorial research draft.
